text.title: Customer Success Basics for Solopreneurs Worked Example
text.summary: One worked example walking from inputs through the procedure to a validated `spec` artefact. Illustrates how the rules in 01-core-rules.xml constrain the output and how the validator behaves on an OK input. Onboarding playbook, at-risk intervention, expansion path, and worked examples for SaaS and course products.

list.item: Trigger: scheduled cadence (quarter-start review).
Owner: named human with role and signoff authority.
Evidence: at least one link with a claim string ≥ 3 chars.
Prior artefact (optional): previous instance for diff.

section.title: Worked artefact (abbreviated)

list.item: Run: python3 scripts/validate-ops-customer-success-basics.py --file artefact.json → exit 0, prints OK.
Mutate `owner` to a string `"team"` → exit 1, prints VIOLATION lines for `$.owner: expected object`.
Run python3 scripts/validate-ops-customer-success-basics.py --self-test → exit 0 against the embedded fixtures.

section.title: Outcome review
section.p: After two cadence cycles, compare the operating signal targeted by this methodology against baseline. If the artefact did not change behaviour, propose deprecation per step 7 of the procedure.

example.title: SaaS team collaboration tool
example.note: SaaS team collaboration tool. Success definition: team uses daily, 3+ active projects, 80%+ adoption. Playbook: Day 1 admin onboarding call; Day 7 team training webinar; Day 14 check-in email; Day 30 success review call; Monthly usage report; Quarterly business review. All touchpoints event-triggered where possible (e.g. Day 7 webinar invite only if team has less than 3 projects).

example.title: Online course
example.note: Online course. Success definition: complete 80% of content, implement learnings, achieve stated goal. Playbook: Day 1 welcome + learning roadmap; Day 3 first module completion reminder (if not started); Weekly progress email; Module completion acknowledgment + next steps; Completion survey + testimonial request.

section.title: Touchpoint design
section.p: Event-triggered touchpoint schedule per rule r2 — each line names the product event that fires it:

list.item: New customer: Day 1 welcome → Day 3 check-in (if no key action) → Day 7 progress → Day 14 feature tip → Day 30 success review
No login for 7 days: re-engagement email with one specific tip tied to their last action
No login for 14 days: personal outreach from founder/CSM
Usage approaching plan limit: proactive upgrade offer with value framing
First success milestone: celebrate + identify next goal + natural expansion conversation

section.title: At-risk intervention
section.p: Health-band response, bounded by the re-engagement cap in rule r4:

list.item: Health band red (score below 50): immediate CSM review, personal outreach within 24 hours
Health band yellow (score 50-74): automated email with specific tip, monitor for 7 days, escalate if no improvement
Health band green (score 75+): maintain regular cadence, watch for expansion signals
Customer hitting plan limits → proactive upgrade offer before they feel blocked
Adding team members → invite prompt for additional seats
Using advanced features → showcase premium tier that extends those features
Requesting a feature → show existing solution + note if upgrade unlocks more
Success milestone reached → celebrate + cross-sell related product

text.reference: Customer health score: usage (40) + adoption (30) + sentiment (20) + billing (10)
